decisions.proposal: All capability, scenario, operation and contract IDs and all JSON member names in this pack are proposed authoring identities, not an observed estate binding. Requests exclude caller-supplied roles. Generated IDs in fixtures are controlled test values, not a mandated production allocation algorithm.

Use a provider-neutral identityResponseRef resolved and validated server-side. The existing DNR identity technology, protocol, registration screens, session mechanism and claim mapping are unknown. Do not add a password database or assume a vendor.

Proposed: remove a definition or attribute from active discovery/selection while retaining historical references. Definition removal does not delete prior encounters or teams. Referenced selectable values cannot be removed without an explicit migration decision. Confirm this retention policy; it is not in the brief.

Proposed: case-insensitive common-name substring match, with an all-digit query also matching an exact collection number. Do not use locked scientific/attribute data as a search side channel. Fuzzy search, stemming and translated search behavior remain undecided.

Proposed: personal collections, encounter media and team mutations are scoped to the server-validated subject. A biologist can edit the catalog but cannot thereby read or change another user's private collection. Public/anonymous catalog access is not settled.

Proposed: team membership refers to collected encounter instances, not species definitions; the same encounter cannot appear twice. Distinct instances of the same definition are allowed. One submitted list replaces the team atomically, and an empty list clears it. Confirm these semantics.

Proposed: encounterId is a stable client-generated key scoped to the authenticated user. The same key and same canonical request returns the existing encounter; the same key with changed content is refused. Different keys remain distinct encounters even when every wildlife field matches.

The state, counties, full 15-type catalog, stat names/value domains and animal dataset are not supplied. Fixture values are synthetic only. Proposed: public collection numbers are unique; referenced counties/types/attributes/values must exist in the selected reference catalog. No unrequested stat scale is imposed.

Candidate only: a previously signed-in user with a cached catalog can retain a local draft with its photo and location, see that it is pending, and synchronize it later under the same subject. No cross-device, first-visit-offline or background-sync guarantee is made. Conflict and retention details require owner decisions.

Proposed test contract accepts image bytes and returns an owned media reference; production upload transport, allowed formats, size limits, privacy, retention and malware controls remain undecided. Image acceptance is not species verification. No upload-size limit is invented.

en and es plus the fixture viewport sizes are test examples, not the state's chosen languages or mandated breakpoints. UI labels and domain descriptions need an explicit translation policy. Accessibility and responsive behavior require rendered-surface assessment, not just a returned declaration.

The brief supplies population/concurrency and a WCAG version/level, but no latency/error/availability targets, load mix, browser versions or accessibility audit method. Record these before certifying readiness. The quality plan does not invent service-level numbers.
Proposed: definition, attribute and team replacement requests carry expectedRevision. A stale revision refuses without overwriting newer state. This concurrency policy is not specified in the brief.

Proposed: collected individuals are returned in ascending encounterId order; team members preserve the submitted selection order; resolved attributeDetails are ordered by attributeId, except where an explicitly named fixture subset contains one attribute. Only definition collection-number ordering is supplied by Nerdery. Confirm or replace these proposed tie-breaks before admission.
